steps.title: Grow Arabidopsis plants for imaging
steps.instruction: Sow Arabidopsis thaliana Col‑0 seeds (carrying a plasma‑membrane fluorescent marker) in wet soil pots, spacing seeds at least 5 cm apart (five seeds per pot: one in each corner and one in the centre). Place pots in trays with a 1 cm water layer, cover with lids and vernalize at 4 °C for 48 h. Transfer trays to a growth chamber set to long‑day (16 h light, ~150 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹), 60–70 % relative humidity, 22 ± 1 °C. After ~7 days (first two true leaves visible) remove lids. Water trays every other day with ~1 cm water. Plants typically bolt after ~3 weeks and are ready for dissection at ~4 weeks.

steps.title: Prepare 1/2 MS agar plates
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 L 1/2 MS medium by mixing 2.15 g Murashige‑Skoog basal salts, 10 g sucrose, 1 mL MS vitamin solution, and 15 g agar; adjust pH to 5.8 with NaOH/HCl and add deionized H₂O to 1 L. Autoclave at 120 °C for 30 min. After cooling to ~50 °C, add 1 mL plant preservative mixture (PPM) per L to obtain a 0.1 % PPM solution. Under a laminar flow cabinet, dispense 1/2–2/3 of each 35 × 10 mm Petri dish with the medium and allow to solidify. Wrap plates with Parafilm, store at 4 °C (up to 3 months).

steps.title: Equilibrate plates and sterilize tools
steps.instruction: Bring the prepared 1/2 MS plates to room temperature before use. Clean the dissection workspace, tweezers, scalpel blades, and 25 G × 1 in. syringe needles with 70 % ethanol solution. Place a Kimwipe moistened with deionized H₂O on the stereomicroscope stage (use only enough water to keep tissue moist; re‑apply when dry).

steps.title: Select and pre‑condition inflorescences
steps.instruction: Choose 4‑week‑old plants that have an inflorescence bearing ~10 mature siliques. Ensure the plants are well‑watered the day before dissection.

steps.title: Add PPM solution and equilibrate sample
steps.instruction: Fill the cut‑out chamber (or hole) with the 0.1 % PPM solution, ensuring the dissected sample is completely submerged. If a bubble appears in front of the organ of interest, use a 200 µL pipette tip aimed at the bud and gently pipette to dislodge the bubble. Let the sample sit in the solution for 5–10 min to stabilize before imaging.

steps.title: Set up confocal microscope and acquire images
steps.instruction: Place the Petri dish on the confocal stage and adjust the dish holder. Use a long‑working‑distance water‑immersion objective (e.g., W Plan‑Apochromat 40×/1.0, NA > 0.8). Excite the plasma‑membrane YFP with a 488 nm diode laser and collect emission at 500–600 nm. steps.title: Verify 3D stack quality
steps.instruction: After acquisition, open the 3D display tool in the imaging software to inspect the stack for realistic organ shape. If sample movement is observed (e.g., deformation, flattening), check the anti‑vibration platform and ensure the 5–10 min incubation was respected. If movement persists, transfer the sample to a freshly cut chamber (see mounting step) and reposition the stem.
